opportunities.title: No published LLM benchmark results
opportunities.detail: Neither of the two multilingual benchmarks we track reports this language. Adding it would give builders and buyers a baseline.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years. Ready to use: FLORES-200 (covers this language); Belebele (covers this language).

opportunities.title: A spell-checker could be built from open text
opportunities.detail: No spell-checker was found. FineWeb-2 holds about 19 million words of open web text, enough for a first word list.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years. Ready to use: FineWeb-2 (19 million words); Wikipedia (2 thousand articles).

opportunities.title: No major platform or open project offers this interface language
opportunities.detail: Phones and computers can't be set to this language, so every app is used in a second language.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years. Ready to use: Unicode CLDR (basic coverage); FineWeb-2 (19 million words).

opportunities.title: No published speech recognition error rate
opportunities.detail: The language isn't in the published FLEURS error-rate breakdowns we track, so builders can't tell how usable open speech recognition is.
opportunities.why: About 9.2 million Oromo speakers are online today, and that should reach 13 million within five years. Ready to use: WAXAL (223 hours of transcribed speech); YODAS2 (16 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: No cloud text-to-speech voice found, though open resources exist
opportunities.detail: None of the cloud services checked has a voice for this language. An open text-to-speech model already speaks it. Open datasets hold 276 hours of transcribed speech.
opportunities.why: About 9.2 million Oromo speakers are online today, and that should reach 13 million within five years. Ready to use: MMS text-to-speech (covers this language); WAXAL (223 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: Speech input is offered by 1 of 4 major services
opportunities.detail: Some services already recognise this language. Open training data includes 276 hours of transcribed speech across 4 open datasets.
opportunities.why: About 9.2 million Oromo speakers are online today, and that should reach 13 million within five years. Ready to use: WAXAL (223 hours of transcribed speech); YODAS2 (16 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: No text recognition, open or commercial
opportunities.detail: Printed books, signs and forms can't be read by phone cameras or digitised at scale.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years.

opportunities.title: Locale data in Unicode CLDR is basic
opportunities.detail: Complete CLDR data (names, dates, numbers, character sets) underpins interface localisation, keyboards and reading numbers aloud in text-to-speech.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years. Ready to use: Unicode CLDR (basic coverage).

opportunities.title: Translation is offered by 2 of 3 major services
opportunities.detail: An open model and the FLORES-200 evaluation set already cover this language, so the main remaining step is a product launch.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years. Ready to use: NLLB-200 (covers this language); FLORES-200 (covers this language).

opportunities.title: Wikipedia has 28 active editors
opportunities.detail: A small editing community limits new open text. Edit-a-thons and translation drives with universities have grown communities elsewhere.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years.

opportunities.title: A keyboard layout exists but isn't on every major platform
opportunities.detail: A layout ships on 2 of 3 major keyboards. Contributing it to CLDR Keyboards, the open interchange format for layouts, would let any platform adopt it.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years. Ready to use: Keyman keyboards (covers this language); Unicode CLDR (basic coverage).

opportunities.title: Only about 19 million words of open web text
opportunities.detail: Little text online limits language models and word prediction. Digitising books and news archives is often the fastest route.
opportunities.why: About 4.8 million Oromo speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.8 million within five years.
